sections.title: Sounds of lk
paragraphs: The spelling -lk sounds like the sound /k/. You hear it in (walk) /wɔːk/, which means to walk. This letter group makes two different sounds in English words.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof. Stop the air, then release it with a sharp burst. Your vocal cords stay still. For the second sound, first touch the roof with your tongue tip. Let air flow around the sides, then make that sharp burst.

sections.title: Reading the spelling
paragraphs: At the end of words where the first letter is silent, you say the sound /k/. You hear this pattern in (talk) /tɔːk/. After vowels where both letters are sounded, you say the sound /lk/. You hear this in (milk) /mɪlk/ and in (silk) /sɪlk/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not pronounce the first letter in words where it stays quiet. Keep the sound simple and clean. Make the sharp burst at the very end.
